solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Forced point following endless waffle

indicators.note: following says the compass point comes after the trimmed waffle
endless says the word for waffle loses its final letter

parts.note: waffle, as idle talk, is drivel
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone pressed into a position after a rambling, interminable speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the L from DRIVEL, leaving DRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven and forced are synonyms as past participles: pushed or compelled by pressure.

clue.text: Difference of opinion in group

definitions.meaning: a ... is a disagreement, as in a ... in the party
a ... is a section or unit of an organisation, such as a league ...

explanation.surface: Disagreement within a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Division covers both a split between people and a section into which things are grouped.

clue.text: Short story about soldier in pub's nonsense

indicators.note: about says the shortened story is turned round
short says the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a story can be a lie

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the pub

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a pub tells a tall tale that makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims LIE to LI, and 'about' turns it to IL. The definition is an adjective: 'pub's nonsense' means the pub is nonsensical.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical means lacking sense or reason, which is what nonsense describes; here 'nonsense' acts adjectivally.

clue.text: Knock back beer and start on neat spirit

indicators.note: knock back, as in sending back, says the beer word is reversed

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Downing a pint and then a neat shot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' looks like drinking but reverses ALE to ELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and vigour, a lively spirit in doing something.

clue.text: Divulge, and indeed question, article about island

indicators.note: about says the act is wrapped around the remaining pieces

parts.note: read as 'in deed': a deed is an act
a is the indefinite article
N is a short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: Someone told to reveal things, and indeed to ask about an article concerning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'indeed' must be split as 'in deed' to give an act; 'and' supplies N, the 'n' of rock 'n' roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with facts is to make them known, so it serves as a synonym of divulge, to disclose.

clue.text: Spaniel fed heartily on large male bird

parts.note: a cocker is a breed of spaniel

indicators.note: heartily takes the heart, the middle letter, of fed

explanation.surface: A spaniel fed generously on a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a young rooster, the male of the domestic fowl.

clue.text: In France, a former policeman's taken over rape case not yet investigated

parts.note: un is French for a
ex means former

indicators.note: taken over says the policeman takes the case letters into himself

parts.note: plod is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: In France, an ex-cop has taken over a rape case still unexamined.
explanation.walkthrough: PC Plod is the policeman in the Noddy children's books, hence British slang for any officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexplored means not yet examined or looked into, so it matches not yet investigated.

clue.text: Addition's complicated and not for dunce

indicators.note: complicated says the letters are tangled into a new order
not says the letters of and are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Adding up is too complicated for a slow pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDITION less A, N, D leaves DITIO, which 'complicated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a foolish person, a synonym of dunce.

clue.text: Grumpy having to engrave inside edges of trophy

indicators.note: inside places the engraving word within the trophy's edges
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to etch is to engrave

explanation.surface: A craftsman irritable at having to engrave around a trophy's rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable and bad-tempered, a synonym of grumpy.

clue.text: Tees off with middle of fairway drive

indicators.note: off, as in gone wrong, says the letters of tees are rearranged
the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A golfer tees off and drives down the centre of the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees off' looks like starting a golf hole, but 'off' rearranges TEES.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a vehicle is to drive it, guiding its direction.

clue.text: Brave boxer put in against six-footer

indicators.note: put in says the boxer's name is placed inside the other two pieces

parts.note: V, for versus, means against
an ant is an insect, with six legs, so a six-footer
Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A courageous fighter set against a tall opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Valiant and brave are synonyms describing courage in the face of danger.

clue.text: Boots maybe for man pursuing lead in cowboy film

indicators.note: pursuing says the man comes after the cowboy's first letter
the lead in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
a film is a thin layer, like a mist

explanation.surface: Footwear for a man chasing the star of a western movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British pharmacy chain, so it is an example of a chemist; 'Boots' looks like footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is a well-known British high-street pharmacy, an example of a dispensing shop; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Notice some training issues in review

indicators.note: in review means the hidden letters are looked back over, read backwards
some says only part of the following words' letters is taken

explanation.surface: A notice about training problems that are being reviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a posted notice giving information or warning, so the nouns match.

clue.text: High excitement always after kick-off in Fulham ground

indicators.note: after places always behind the first letter of Fulham
the kick-off in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'
a pitch is a sports ground

explanation.surface: A football crowd's frenzy at the start of a match at Fulham's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is an idiom for a state of intense excitement or agitation.

clue.text: Flying high above earth, awfully thin atmosphere

parts.note: up means above

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of thin are badly jumbled

parts.note: E is the electrical abbreviation for earth
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: An aircraft soaring above the ground in rarefied air.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the air literally describes something aloft, as in flying high; it also means undecided.

clue.text: Fill retired commanding officer's mug with last of brandy

indicators.note: retired, as in withdrawn backwards, says the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a mug is a cup

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of brandy

explanation.surface: A retired army officer topping up his mug with the dregs of the brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a space is to fill it, as in occupying a seat or one's time.

clue.text: Offends boyfriend returning 40% of gifts

indicators.note: returning says the word for boyfriend is read backwards

parts.note: a boyfriend is a lover

indicators.note: forty per cent of a five-letter word is two of its letters, here the closing two

explanation.surface: A boyfriend causes offence by sending back a share of the presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LOVER into REVOL; '40% of' gifts takes its last two letters, TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust or offend them, so both are transitive verbs of causing distaste.

clue.text: Surprise stand by America on aid

parts.note: to stand something is to take or tolerate it
to back someone is to support or aid them

explanation.surface: America's stance on foreign aid comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aback is an idiom meaning to shock or surprise someone.

clue.text: Rescue dog has missing tail

indicators.note: missing its tail says the dog word loses its final letter

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A rescue dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve something is to recover or rescue it, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Loses temper over sexy photo

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to snap is to lose one's temper suddenly
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage about a racy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.

clue.text: Arranged for personal contents to be removed before old queen died

indicators.note: before puts the shell of personal ahead of the queen
removing the contents of personal leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Someone's personal belongings cleared out before an old queen's death, as organised.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSONAL with its middle removed leaves PL.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned and arranged are synonyms meaning organised in advance.

clue.text: Jog wearing gilet

parts.note: to jog is to jerk or nudge
in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'

explanation.surface: Going for a run dressed in a sleeveless top.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless jacket, much like a gilet, a padded sleeveless waistcoat.

clue.text: Look! Old book's turned up in summerhouse

parts.note: to gaze is to look

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, says the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone spots an old book that has turned up in a garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, a kind of summerhouse.

clue.text: Trolls take on reserve after own goal

indicators.note: after says the reserve comes behind the own goal

explanation.surface: Internet trolls mock a substitute brought on after a team's own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres and trolls are both monstrous creatures from folklore.

clue.text: Everything about her, time and time again, is really fashionable

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: about says the two time words go around her

parts.note: the second time is an age, a long stretch of time; 'again' marks the repeat

explanation.surface: Praise for someone whose style keeps being in vogue again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and time again' gives two different words for time, the short abbreviation and then a long stretch; 'again' just marks the repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: All the rage is an idiom meaning currently very popular or in vogue.

clue.text: Vegetables and cooked eels contain potassium

indicators.note: contain says the jumbled eels hold the potassium symbol
cooked says the letters of eels are mixed up

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A dish of vegetables and stewed eels, rich in potassium.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeks are vegetables of the onion family, an example of the class.

clue.text: Distort sample from slow arpeggio

indicators.note: sample from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician distorting a passage taken from a slow broken chord.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp something is to bend it out of shape, a synonym of distort.

clue.text: Intelligent questions on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: whys are questions, as in the whys and wherefores

explanation.surface: Clever questions asked on a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise and intelligent are synonyms describing someone with good judgement and understanding.

clue.text: Lift broken, leave note

indicators.note: broken says the letters of leave are shattered and reassembled

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The lift is out of order, so leave a message saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift and to elevate are synonymous verbs meaning to raise up.

clue.text: Talk about life — what about mine with a prince?

indicators.note: about says the exclamation wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A question about a royal mining heir's biography.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is a short tribute to the dead, a few words summing up a life, often on a gravestone.

clue.text: Studied irregular verbs in reference work

indicators.note: in places the jumbled verbs inside the dictionary

parts.note: the OED, Oxford English Dictionary, is a reference work

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of verbs are disordered

explanation.surface: A grammar student looking up irregular verbs in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully or examine, so observed works as a past-tense synonym of studied.

clue.text: Rip packet and eat a little bit

indicators.note: rip, as tearing apart, says the letters of packet are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tearing open a packet and nibbling the contents.
explanation.definitionFit: To peck at food is an idiom for eating only small amounts without appetite.
